title: Responses v3 compatibility shim: resilient stream stitching, function-call fidelity, and deterministic-seed propagation
author: Priya Raman
description: Introduces a compatibility shim and runtime fixes to support an evolving Responses v3 streaming envelope used by OpenAI-compatible clients. This PR addresses three user-visible classes of issues observed under load: (1) fragmented streaming frames that split UTF-8 token boundaries or split function_call tool frames which caused out-of-order assembly, (2) loss or mutation of function_call intent during gateway->router->worker handoffs and cross-region fallbacks, and (3) client-specified seed/determinism flags and arbitrary response-level metadata not being forwarded into the serving pipeline or audit rows. The implementation normalizes incoming v3 envelopes into a compact internal event model, provides a deterministic reassembly algorithm that stitches partial byte sequences and tool frames, serializes function_call intent into the routing context to survive asynchronous queuing and fallbacks, and attaches client seed and metadata to the request context and audit enrichment. The feature is behind a runtime flag openai_responses_v3_compat and gated by an explicit client-version header so that older traffic is unaffected. Rollout plan: dark-launch 10% traffic, staging dogfood with end-to-end tracing, canary ramp to 50% then promote after 48 hours of stability. Includes unit/fuzz tests for reassembly invariants, an integration fallback scenario to validate header preservation, SDK adapters in TypeScript/Python, CI pipeline additions, and docs for SDK consumers and operator flags.

release_notes: Adds a compatibility shim for Responses v3 streaming envelopes: deterministic streaming reassembly for partial UTF-8 and split tool frames, preserved function_call header semantics across routing and fallbacks, and client seed/response metadata passthrough into audit logs. Feature is opt-in via openai_responses_v3_compat and client-version header.
